evidence: WHAT HOLDS: All five prompts open the live app with the browser tool on line 1: 'Open http://localhost:3000 using Playwright.' (tests/gates/render/prompt.md:1, gates/constraints/prompt.md:1, scored/functional/prompt.md:1, scored/polish/prompt.md:1, scored/visual/prompt.md:1). Each forbids source scoring: 'Use rendered UI and ordinary browser-observed product data only. Never inspect app source, bundles, filesystem, database files or implementation code. No shell or private-file probes.' All five judge.toml files declare [[judge.mcp_servers]] name='playwright', command='playwright-mcp' (line 8-12 each) with prompt_template='prompt.md'; functional adds the verifier restart server (judge.toml:14-18). app_context.md:4 'URL: http://localhost:3000' matches test.sh port 3000 and is substituted into every prompt by test.sh:196-200. First-paint guessing is excluded: render gate requires a wrong-password refusal then a real sign-in to a usable workspace ('A static picture or only a health response is insufficient', render judge.toml:23); constraints, functional, polish and visual all restate a minimal backend gate that creates a job+candidate via UI and reads it back as the Observer in an independent context ('A static page, a no-op save or a browser-only save fails this check', functional prompt.md:11, polish :11, visual :11). Criteria are phrased as live browser observations (protocol steps S..D, document.activeElement, 15-second no-reload waits, replays of observed requests). Visual likert rows are scored from rendered surfaces after a scripted read-only tour (visual prompt.md:14). Four of five prompts also carry an explicit memory/guess guard: 'If an evaluator/tool failure or exhausted budget prevents the gate or an owned observation, return binary0 for the unobserved outcome with reason "NOT EXERCISED - evaluator/tool limitation"' (render:11, constraints:11, polish:18, visual:16 with Likert1). DEFECT: tests/scored/functional/prompt.md, the heaviest dimension (41 criteria, 13 sequential protocols Z,S,M,L,C,B,N,T,U,K,R,V,A,D, timeout 9000 s in judge.toml:4), carries NO equivalent unobserved-outcome rule: grep for 'NOT EXERCISED|budget|unattempted|did not perform|evidence you' over the task prompts matches functional only at line 7 ('If a feature does not work as delivered, give that criterion its lowest score'), which covers an OBSERVED failure, not an unperformed step. The template's functional prompt had exactly this guard ('A criterion passes only on evidence you gathered yourself in this session ... If you did not perform a step, that step did not pass ... Never fabricate a pass. If you run out of budget with criteria unattempted, mark them failed', template scored/functional/prompt.md:17-21); the task replaced that section and did not carry the guard into functional while adding it to the other four. Only hro_restart has a row-specific not-performed rule (functional prompt.md:51). In batched mode the judge must emit a verdict for every criterion, so late-protocol rows (N, T, U, K, R, V, A) can be filled in from impressions of earlier protocols or general expectation rather than a live observation. RUN EVIDENCE: raw-evidence-index.json scope states 'Full configured grading/workload ... are absent' and the golden driver 'does not walk every Functional criterion as the judge would'; no configured judge trajectory exists to show the judge actually used the browser for each row or how it handled budget exhaustion. browser_run_code_unsafe availability in @playwright/mcp@0.0.79 (used for independent contexts) was not verified by me (tool feasibility belongs to other rows; noted only).
counterexample: Broken app that could pass: an app whose board, moves and sign-in work but whose candidate privacy, Activity log and notes permissions are broken (e.g. Activity omits undo lines, candidate responses leak internal notes). The functional judge spends its 9000 s budget on protocols S, M, L, C and B (many replays and independent contexts) and runs out before N, K, R, A. Because the functional prompt, unlike the other four prompts and unlike the template, never says that an unperformed step is 0/NOT EXERCISED, the batched judge still must return all 41 verdicts and may infer passes for hro_activity, hro_candidate_private, hro_notes, hro_observer_readonly from the app's evident overall quality - scoring from memory/guess rather than the live browser, inflating up to ~13 weight units of functional reward (hro_candidate_private 2.5 + hro_activity 1 + hro_notes 1 + hro_observer_readonly 1 + hro_anonymous 1.5 + hro_candidate_view 1.5 + hro_candidate_no_staff 1 + hro_mgr_* 3 ...). Conversely, a conforming app could be scored 0 or 1 inconsistently on unreached rows depending on the judge's improvisation, adding variance unrelated to the submission.
suggested_fix: Add to tests/scored/functional/prompt.md the same paragraph the other four prompts already carry: 'If an evaluator/tool failure or exhausted budget prevents the gate or an owned observation, return binary0 for the unobserved outcome with reason "NOT EXERCISED - evaluator/tool limitation". This is missing evidence, not an observed application failure. Preserve every completed independent observation.' (prompt-only change; no harness or reward policy edit), then re-run the deterministic check-rubric-prompt review on the new candidate.
